# Intake Brief: Audit freshness invalidates only on this work item's own data change

## Problem statement

The audit freshness gate invalidates a stored audit when ANY of its content-fingerprint components change: git HEAD sha, work-item description hash, Key Files list, and working-tree state (`git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD`). Because the fingerprint includes the **whole-repo** git HEAD sha and working-tree state, a commit to dev from an *unrelated* work item (or any uncommitted/untracked file change) invalidates every stored audit in the worklog and re-triggers the full audit pipeline — even though the audited item itself never changed.

**Observed failure (SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0):** the item was audited "Ready to close: Yes" at HEAD `310773d5`. Afterward, an unrelated work item (SA-0MSQ026T3009QY2L) merged `aaabdede` to dev. The content fingerprint changed (verified: stored `58947e06…` matches recomputation at `310773d5` but not at `aaabdede`), so the audit went stale, the re-audit ran, and it blocked on the pre-flight full-suite cache gate — leaving a verified "Ready to close: Yes" item stuck in review.

## Users

- Audit operators / automated dispatchers relying on `audit_runner.py` freshness short-circuit (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) to skip re-audits of unchanged items.

**User story:** "As an audit operator, I want a stored audit to remain valid unless THIS work item's own data changes, so unrelated repository activity doesn't invalidate my audits."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_compute_content_fingerprint` is computed from the **work item's own data only** — the work item's description (which contains the ACs and the Key Files section) plus its title. The **git HEAD sha and working-tree-state components are removed** from the fingerprint entirely (no git calls in the computation).
2. A git HEAD move caused by ANY other work item's commit does **not** invalidate a stored audit of an item whose own data is unchanged. Regression test: fingerprint is stable when only the HEAD sha differs (item data identical).
3. Uncommitted and untracked working-tree changes do **not** invalidate a stored audit. Regression test: fingerprint is stable across `git status --porcelain` / `git diff --name-only HEAD` differences.
4. A change to this item's own data (title / description / ACs / Key Files section) after the audit **does** invalidate and re-runs the pipeline (existing description/key-files fingerprint tests remain green).
5. Comments, status/stage/priority/assignee changes, and sortIndex changes do **not** invalidate (they move `updatedAt` but are not audited content).
6. **Migration of legacy v1 reports:** reports persisted before this change carry fingerprints computed with the git-inclusive formula that cannot be recomputed. Version the fingerprint line (e.g. `Audit content fingerprint (v2): <hash>`) so legacy lines are distinguishable; legacy reports fall back to the existing time-gate floor (auditedAt vs updatedAt + `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS`) — **no silent mass re-audit wave** of the existing in_review backlog. Document the one-time re-audit consequence for legacy items whose `updatedAt` moved after the audit, and its interaction with the pre-flight full-suite cache gate.
7. Dead code cleanup: `_resolve_working_tree_hash` (only used by the fingerprint) is removed; `_resolve_audited_head` stays (still used by green-run attestation).
8. Documentation updated: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (freshness-gate section ~line 134), `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~line 95), and the code docstrings on `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` / `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`. Full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** the rule is about *when an existing audit is reused*, never about what the audit concludes. `--force` still bypasses the gate.
- **Read-only:** the fingerprint change must not execute the test suite or make any pi calls.
- **No regression in the freshness skip:** items whose data is unchanged still short-circuit in seconds (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT intent preserved).
- **Fail-open preserved:** any failure to compute the new fingerprint still falls through to a full re-audit (existing behavior).
- **Child reuse gate:** child-audit reuse (LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR, lines ~3877/6056/6391) uses the same fingerprint — it must keep working with the simplified formula (children's own data unchanged → reused).

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`:
  - `_compute_content_fingerprint` (line ~1034) — payload = `{head_sha, description_hash, key_files, working_tree_hash}`.
  - `_check_audit_freshness` (line ~913) — content gate primary; time gate floor for fingerprint-less legacy reports.
  - `_resolve_working_tree_hash` (line ~1080) — only used by the fingerprint (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ).
  - `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = "Audit content fingerprint: "` (line 431); embedded at lines ~3256/3281/3538.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — fingerprint tests at ~7791-7913 (HEAD sha, description, key files, working-tree states), freshness-gate tests (~2252, 3798-3813, 4275).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness gate behavior section (line ~134).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness gate summary (line ~95).
- Related (separate repo, out of scope): herdr downtime worker's dispatcher-side `isAuditFresh` (ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`, time-based `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`) caused the re-dispatch that exposed this; covered by RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT (ContextHub worklog).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_compute_content_fingerprint` (simplify), `_check_audit_freshness` (versioned-line handling), `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, remove `_resolve_working_tree_hash`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — update fingerprint/freshness tests (~7791-7913, 2252, 3798-3813, 4275)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate section
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — freshness-gate summary line

## Related work

- `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` — Include working-tree state in the audit content fingerprint (in_review) — the working-tree component this item REMOVES (this item supersedes that component).
- `SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT` — Audit: content-based freshness gate (done) — introduced the fingerprint; this item simplifies its scope.
- `SA-0MSN04X2S006ONH0` — Audit runner: detect proxy 'cheap' mode (in_review) — the item whose blocked re-audit exposed this problem.
- `WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT` — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (ContextHub worklog) — dispatcher-side re-dispatch trigger; separate concern.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "this work item's data":** title + description (ACs + Key Files section). Comments, lifecycle fields, and repo state are NOT audited content and must not invalidate.
- **Assumption — migration via versioned line:** legacy v1 reports fall back to the time gate (existing floor for fingerprint-less reports). A legacy item whose `updatedAt` moved after its audit is re-audited once, then stores a v2 fingerprint and is immune to comment/HEAD churn thereafter. Accepted: this is a one-time, bounded transition.
- **Risk — stale code evidence:** dropping the git components means a stored audit may reference code that changed under it (e.g. another work item edits a Key File). Accepted by design per this item's rule; the audit's verdict remains the record for the item's own data.
- **Risk — herdr re-dispatch noise:** herdr may still dispatch /skill:audit for items whose `updatedAt` moved; with this fix the runner short-circuits ("Skipping: audit still fresh", zero pi calls). Dispatcher-side change is out of scope (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should a git HEAD move from another work item invalidate this item's audit? — Answer (user): No. "An audit is only invalidated if there is a change to this work item's data AFTER the audit was created." The rule is that simple.
- Q: What about the working-tree component (SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ)? — Answer: remove it too — same reasoning (repo state, not item data). This item supersedes SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ's component.
- Q: Do comments / status / stage changes invalidate? — Answer (assumed, per rule): no — they are not this item's audited data. Document as an explicit decision.
- Q: Migration of existing stored fingerprints? — Answer (assumed): version the fingerprint line so legacy reports are distinguishable; legacy → existing time-gate floor; no mass re-audit wave.

# Intake Draft — Audit: on ruff false positive, fix the ruff config and re-run (justified READ-ONLY break)

**Work item:** SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR
**Type:** feature | **Priority:** critical (operator-specified)

## Headline

When the audit's Phase 1 code-quality scan surfaces a ruff finding that a model-judged screen confidently identifies as a **false positive**, the audit applies a minimal ruff-config fix in the audited project, commits it (tracked by a newly created work item), re-hashes the content fingerprint, and re-runs only the code-quality scan. Uncertain findings are never auto-changed — they stay as findings annotated "candidate false positive — producer decision required". This is an explicit, justified exception to the audit's READ-ONLY rule.

## Problem statement

The audit skill's Phase 1 code-quality check runs ruff over the scoped changed-file list and classifies findings by severity (`_classify_ruff`). False positives — findings that are not genuine problems (e.g. the EXE001 severity misclassification, SA-0MSG83Z4Z004YH2P) — surface as critical/high findings that block closure and waste review cycles. Today each false positive is fixed once, manually, by editing the skill's severity map. There is no general mechanism for the audit to recognize a false positive, remediate it at the source (the project's ruff config), and re-verify.

## Users

- **Audit runner / release pipeline** — wants audits to converge without being blocked by non-issues, while never masking genuine findings.
- **Work-item producer** — wants visibility and control: no config change without a confident model judgment; doubt cases surfaced for producer decision; every config change tracked in its own work item with the commit.

### Example user stories

- *As the audit runner, when ruff flags a file with a rule that is a known misfire for that file, I want the audit to add a `per-file-ignore` to the project's ruff config and re-run the scan so the audit converges without a false blocking finding.*
- *As a producer, when the model is unsure whether a finding is a false positive, I want the finding retained and annotated "candidate false positive — producer decision required" so nothing is changed without my confirmation.*
- *As a reviewer, when the audit applies a config change, I want it tracked in its own work item with the commit link so the change is visible and reviewable.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **False-positive screen:** ruff findings from the Phase 1 code-quality scan are classified by a model-judged screen into `genuine` / `confident-false-positive` / `uncertain`, each with a written justification recorded in the audit report. The screen errs on the side of caution.
2. **Confident remediation loop:** for `confident-false-positive` findings only, the audit applies a minimal ruff config change to the audited project (`per-file-ignores` or rule exclusion in `pyproject.toml`/`ruff.toml`; the file is created if none exists), commits it, **re-hashes the content fingerprint** (preventing freshness-gate invalidation from the dirty tree), and re-runs **only the code-quality scan** — the pipeline is not restarted. The loop is capped at 3 config-fix iterations per audit run.
3. **Uncertain findings untouched:** `uncertain` findings are never auto-changed; they remain findings annotated "candidate false positive — producer decision required" and continue to block closure under the existing Phase-1 blocking rules (no config change, no commit).
4. **Tracked via a new work item:** each applied config change creates a separate work item (issue-type `chore`) linking the false-positive finding and the commit. The audit's existing prohibition on creating work items is relaxed **only after verifying** the runner's status lifecycle, persistence, and freshness-gate invariants are unaffected (verified by the audit skill test suite — lifecycle, phase1, freshness, core).
5. **Docs + green suite:** the audit SKILL.md (READ-ONLY safety section + the "Do NOT close, create, or delete work items" rule) and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` document the exception and the new behavior; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Ruff only** — eslint and other linters are out of scope for remediation.
- **Config only** — remediation modifies the audited project's ruff config; **no `# noqa` source edits**, no changes to the skill's own severity classifier map (classifier bugs like EXE001 continue to be fixed via normal work items).
- **Erring on the side of caution** — model applies a config fix only when confident; doubt → annotated finding, blocks as today.
- **Minimal, surgical config edits** — targeted at the flagged file(s), not sweeping rule changes; the config work item makes every change visible.
- **READ-ONLY exception scope** — the exception covers only: writing/creating the ruff config file, committing the config fix, creating the config-fix work item, and the code-quality re-run. All other audit phases remain read-only; the audit still does NOT close or delete work items, and never pushes (commit stays local; push follows the normal work-item workflow).
- **Lifecycle integrity** — the config-fix commit and work-item creation must not corrupt the audit's verdict-driven status lifecycle, persistence (readback verification), or freshness gate.

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_phase_fetch_and_cq` runs the scoped code-quality scan: `run_code_quality(project_root=TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT, runner=runner, fix=False, files=cq_scope_files)` — read-only, scoped to the git changed-file list (SA-0MSKB6VWU000RT58).
- Findings are severity-classified by `_classify_ruff` (prefix map in `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py`); critical/high findings block Phase 1 (blocking gate in `_decision_blocking_findings`).
- Audits are strictly read-only except explicit persistence and the automatic status lifecycle; SKILL.md: "Do NOT close, create, or delete work items during an audit."
- Ruff auto-fix (`run_ruff(fix=True)` → `--fix` → rescan, SA-0MQBQDLOY009EO4B) exists but fixes **code**, is not used by audits, and is not config remediation.
- Freshness gate fingerprints HEAD sha + description hash + Key Files + working-tree state (`git status --porcelain`); an uncommitted config edit would dirty the tree and change the fingerprint — hence commit + re-hash.

## Desired change

Insert a model-judged **false-positive screen** between the code-quality scan and the Phase-1 blocking decision. Screen output per ruff finding: `genuine` (keep, current behavior), `confident-false-positive` (propose + apply minimal config remediation, commit, create tracking work item, re-hash fingerprint, re-run code-quality scan only, capped at 3 iterations), `uncertain` (keep finding, annotate "candidate false positive — producer decision required"). Audit report shows the screen classifications and justifications.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase_fetch_and_cq` (scan site), Phase-1 blocking gate, `_compute_content_fingerprint` (re-hash), status lifecycle; new false-positive screen + config-remediation + work-item-creation logic.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — `run_ruff`, `_run_ruff_fix_mode`, `_classify_ruff`; possibly a helper for locating/editing the project's ruff config.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/code_quality.py` — `run_code_quality` orchestrator; may need to expose per-finding linter/rule detail for the screen.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — READ-ONLY safety section + no-create/delete rule → document the justified exception.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — document the screen, remediation loop, and any new flags/env vars (e.g. iteration cap).
- `skill/audit/tests/` — `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`, `test_audit_runner_phase1.py`, `test_audit_runner_freshness.py`, `test_audit_runner_core.py` — new tests for the screen, remediation loop, re-hash, work-item creation, and no-breakage verification.

## Related work

- **SA-0MQBQDLOY009EO4B** — "Add auto-fix support to ruff linter runner" (completed, high): ruff `--fix` + rescan machinery; foundation for fix-then-rescan, but code fixes, not config.
- **SA-0MSG83Z4Z004YH2P** — "EXE001 misclassified as 'high' severity blocks audits on unrelated files" (completed): the motivating false-positive case; fixed once manually in the severity map.
- **SA-0MQA0SDW90056G6O** — "Linting & Severity Classification (Python/TS)" (completed): origin of the severity classifier this screen sits beside.
- **SA-0MQJONW3C007SZQY** — "Audit runner: manage work item status during audit execution" (completed): established the verdict-driven status lifecycle whose invariants must be verified unaffected before relaxing the no-create-work-item restriction (find-related automated report).
- **SA-0MSRLLQ0V008EW3J** — "audit_runner: warn/flag when zero ACs extracted instead of auto-approving" (open, medium): adjacent audit_runner robustness work, not a dependency.
- Automated find-related report (SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51 shared lifecycle scripts, SA-0MSHTRS8F006RUDW Python 3.12 test-failure) — tangential; no impact.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** model proposes sweeping config changes → mitigated by minimal/surgical edits targeted at flagged files, a 3-iteration cap, and full visibility via the tracking work item + commit. Broader refactors are recorded as separate work items, not scope.
- **Over-remediation risk (masking genuine issues):** model over-applies "confident" → mitigated by caution-first instruction, mandatory per-finding justification, cap, and producer review of the tracking work item.
- **No-breakage risk (relaxing no-create-work-item):** work-item creation during audit could interact with lifecycle/persistence/freshness invariants → verified before relaxing (user requirement), covered by the audit test suite.
- **Freshness-gate risk:** config edit dirties the tree → commit + re-hash restores a stable fingerprint.
- **Cost/latency risk:** the false-positive screen adds one Phase-1 Pi call per audit; bounded by the existing per-call budgets and skipped when the scan yields no ruff findings.
- **Assumption:** default remediation cap = 3 config-fix iterations per audit run (configurable).
- **Assumption:** the config-fix commit is local (no push); pushing follows the standard work-item workflow once the config work item is processed.
- **Assumption:** `per-file-ignores` and rule exclusions are the only remediation primitives; severity-map changes to the skill's classifier remain normal work items (EXE001 pattern).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Who determines "false positive"?** — Answer (rgardler): "model judgement, erring on the side of caution, ask producer if in doubt". Final: a model-judged screen classifies findings; caution-first; doubt → producer decision. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2: What does "fix the config" concretely modify?** — Answer (rgardler): "(a) the audited project's ruff config". Final: `pyproject.toml`/`ruff.toml` `per-file-ignores` / rule exclusion only; no `# noqa`, no skill-side classifier changes. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3: Re-run scope and lifecycle?** — Answer (rgardler): "code-quality, but commit and re-hash to prevent invalidation". Final: re-run only the code-quality scan; commit the config fix; recompute the content fingerprint so the freshness gate is stable. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4: "Ask the producer" in an unattended runner?** — Answer (rgardler): "(b) model only applies a config fix when confident; doubt-cases reported as findings annotated 'candidate false positive — producer decision required' (no config change, blocks as today)". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5: Commit hygiene / work-item association?** — Answer (rgardler): "separate item — audits should NOT be forbidden from creating work items, relax that restriction (verifying it doesn't break anything first)". Final: audit creates a `chore` work item per config change; the no-create restriction is relaxed after no-breakage verification. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q6: Config-edit scope (no config file present)?** — Answer (rgardler): "yes, create if needed". Final: the audit may create `pyproject.toml`/`ruff.toml` (or the `[tool.ruff]` section) in the audited project when absent. Source: interactive reply.
- **Issue type / priority (inferred, not asked):** `feature` (net-new audit capability) / `critical` (operator-specified via `--priority critical`).
### Planning session (Plan skill, 2026-08-14)

- **Q7 (remediation scope):** Should config remediation apply to blocking (critical/high) findings only, or to any ruff finding classified confident-false-positive? — Answer (rgardler): "(a) blocking findings only — **work item created for the medium and low pri**". Final: remediation = blocking-severity confident-false-positives only; medium/low confident-false-positives are classified, reported, AND tracked via a chore work item (no config change, no commit link). Source: plan interview reply.
- **Q8 (cap exhaustion):** After the 3-iteration cap, if a finding persists, should it remain a blocking genuine finding or be downgraded? — Answer (rgardler): "(a)". Final: remains a blocking `genuine` finding annotated "remediation loop exhausted". Source: plan interview reply.
- **Q9 (AC4 no-breakage ordering):** Test-first structure confirmed — verification tests (lifecycle/phase1/freshness/core suites) written and green while the no-create restriction is still in force; relaxation lands only with the work-item-creation feature; `wl create` reuses the runner's `_run_wl` with `--worklog-dir` resolution. Answer (rgardler): "confirm". Final: as stated. Source: plan interview reply.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-14 — Planned by `plan` skill: created 7 child work items (test-first) in 4 vertical slices (Screen → Remediation loop → Tracking+relaxation → Docs+green suite); added dependency edges T1→F1, T2→F2, F1→F2, T3→F3, F2→F3, F3→D1; appended Q7–Q9 to the Appendix. Children: Tests: false-positive screen (SA-0MST01NPD007MYG4), False-positive screen (SA-0MST01O4G002VPBR), Tests: config remediation loop (SA-0MST01OIN008MXYT), Config remediation loop (SA-0MST01OX4007Z17C), Tests: no-breakage + chore items (SA-0MST01PBJ008100Y), Work-item creation + no-create relaxation (SA-0MST01PQQ009T0CI), Docs + green suite (SA-0MST01Q4W005G495).

# Intake Brief — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for top-level items (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H)

## Problem Statement

When the audit runner (`audit_runner.py`) completes an audit with a "Ready to close: Yes" verdict, it advances the item to `completed`/`in_review` but does **not** set the `needsProducerReview` flag. The producer-review gate (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` in the ship skill skips items with `needsProducerReview: true`) is therefore bypassed for auto-audited items. However, the flag should only be set for **top-level** items (no parent): child items are covered by their parent's producer review, and marking every child for review would flood the producer queue with redundant approvals. The previous blanket behavior (set the flag for all items, SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW) was dropped during a later refactor (SA-0MS0BP707003KGRM), so this item restores the gating with the top-level-only refinement.

## Users

- **Producers / maintainers** — need assurance that every top-level completed work item proceeds to release only after their explicit review, without being buried by redundant child-item review requests.
- **AI agents running audits** — currently produce `completed` status without the `needsProducerReview` flag, creating a gap in the release gating chain for top-level items.

### User Stories

- **As a** Producer, **I want** every top-level item that an automated audit marks as "ready to close" to also have `needsProducerReview: true`, **so that** I can review it before release.
- **As a** Producer, **I want** child items to be **excluded** from the producer-review flag, **so that** I only review top-level items (their parent's review covers the subtree).
- **As an** AI agent running `/skill:audit`, **I want** the audit runner to set `--needs-producer-review yes` only when the item has no parent, **so that** release gating is enforced without queue flooding.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1**: When `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` in `audit_runner.py` applies a "yes" verdict (`status=completed`, `stage=in_review`) and the audited item has **no parent** (`parentId` is null/empty), the terminal `wl update` includes `--needs-producer-review yes`.
2. **AC2**: When the audited item **has a parent** (`parentId` set), the terminal `wl update` for a "yes" verdict does **not** include `--needs-producer-review` (the flag is left unchanged).
3. **AC3**: The "no" verdict and failure/restore branches never set `--needs-producer-review` (behavior unchanged).
4. **AC4**: Unit tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` verify both cases (top-level sets the flag; child does not), and the full audit test suite passes with no regressions.
5. **AC5**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (Status Lifecycle section) and code comments.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- The change is localized to the standalone audit runner (`audit_runner.py`) — the AMPA engine's audit handler (separate code path, `docs/triage-audit.md`) is unaffected.
- Backward compatibility: the "no" and failure/restore paths must behave exactly as before.
- The flag must be set **only** on a genuine "Yes" verdict for top-level items — never on failure/fallback runs.
- No modifications to `.pi/` or agent-infrastructure directories outside the SorraAgents repo.

## Existing State

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (circa line 6740–6790): the `elif ctx.audit_verdict == "yes":` branch builds `["wl", "update", <id>, "--status", "completed", "--stage", "in_review", "--json"]` — no `--needs-producer-review` flag is ever passed. For `confident-false-positive` ruff findings of blocking severity (critical/high) only: apply a minimal ruff config change to the audited project (create the config file/section if absent), commit it locally, re-hash the content fingerprint, and re-run ONLY the code-quality scan — capped at 3 config-fix iterations per audit run. ## Goal

Prevent the audit runner's Phase-1 code-quality scan from passing non-Python files (YAML, JSON, Markdown, etc.) to ruff as explicit file arguments, eliminating false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that get auto-created as work items.

## Background / Root cause

On 2026-08-11, an implement self-review audit ran `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files)` with the git changed-file list, which included `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (uncommitted changes at the time). `_run_ruff_check` invoked `ruff check <yaml-file>` — ruff parses YAML as Python and emitted 121 false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings, which `create_epics_for_findings` auto-created as work items under the Quality Improvement epic (LP-0MSJFTRUW0076Z5Y). Those stale items were later marked completed/in_review and drained one-by-one by the herdr downtime audit tier (~59 dispatches in one evening).

The `.ruff.toml` `exclude = ["*.yaml", "*.yml"]` fix (commit 7580063) is **insufficient**: ruff only honors `exclude` for directory scans; explicit file arguments bypass it (verified: `ruff check config-cheap.yaml` with the exclude in place still returns invalid-syntax findings, while `ruff check .` returns `[]`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_ruff` / `_run_ruff_check` filter the `files` list to Python extensions (`.py`, `.pyi`, `.ipynb`) before invoking ruff; non-Python files are skipped and never passed as explicit paths.

## Goal

Prevent ruff (the Python linter) from mis-parsing YAML and other non-Python configuration files as Python source, which produces false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that pollute the Quality Improvement epic as auto-created work items. The fix MUST be **additive**: it must not hardcode any project-specific path (e.g. `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`), must not break scanning of other projects, and must never hide genuine Python findings in `.py` files in any project.

## Background / Root cause

The llm project Quality Improvement epic **LP-0MT1F4IQU00828FC** accumulated **155 false-positive child work items** (2026-08-20), all ruff `invalid-syntax` errors reported against `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — a YAML file being linted as Python (Unexpected indentation, Invalid annotated assignment target, Expected an expression, etc.).

The existing explicit-file-argument filter (commit e910f02d, `_run_ruff_check` / `_run_ruff_fix_mode`) only excludes TS/JS extensions and only in the `files=` branch. Two gaps remain:
1. The **whole-project scan path** (`files=None`, the `else` branch) runs `ruff check <root>` with only a TS/JS `--extend-exclude` — it does NOT exclude `.yaml`/`.yml` or other non-Python config files.
2. The current exclusion list is English-agnostic about additivity — it must be extended to cover non-Python config extensions generically so the fix holds for ANY project (not just llm), while never suppressing genuine findings.

Related existing item: **SA-0MSTMAPL40019JX5** addresses the explicit-file-argument path in the audit runner. This item covers the whole-project scan path and generalises the exclusion so it is additive across all projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The whole-project ruff scan path (`files=None`) excludes non-Python configuration extensions (at minimum `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`, `.toml`, `.md`) so ruff never mis-parses them, via `--extend-exclude`/`--force-exclude` — not by hardcoding any project-specific filename.
2. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected: existing tests pass and no Python lint is suppressed.
3. The fix is additive — works for any project root (verified with a non-llm project containing a `.yaml` file), with no hardcoded absolute paths or project names in the exclusion logic.
4. A regression test asserts that scanning a project tree containing a `.yaml` file (both a whole-project scan and an explicit-file scan) produces zero findings for that YAML file, while a `.py` file with a genuine issue still yields its finding.
5. The change is documented in the linter_runner module docstring/comment (both the explicit-file and whole-project paths).

3. Deterministic: same inputs -> same prompt bytes.

5. Skill test suite (skill/agent-log-review/tests) passes; changed-scope suite green.
